title: Sr. Manager, Production Planning & Scheduling
text:
Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future 
 Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.
 
Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.
 
Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.
 
If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.
 
 The Role 
 We're hiring our first Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling to own the factory side execution. Where our S&OP function decides where and whether we can build across the network, you own how and when it actually gets built on the floor. You'll own discrete operational scheduling, job sequencing and priority, and the daily/weekly rhythm that ensures on-time delivery (OTD) and sets the factory up for success.
 This role reports to our Operations leadership and drives a consistent scheduling methodology across the network, while partnering closely with each site General Manager on execution. Your scheduling and planning team members will support the sites day-to-day (dotted-line to the GM) while you own the standards, methodology, and rigor centrally.
 This is a builder and owner role. While the team is built out, you'll be hands-on developing the scheduling methodologies, communication rigor, and visual management that don't exist yet, and turning them into standard work. You'll be the person the floor, Program Management, and leadership rely on for a clear, credible answer to "what are we running, in what order, and are we going to hit the date?"
 You'll partner tightly with the S&OP function, translating network-level allocation and capacity plans into an executable factory schedule — and feeding real execution signal back up to highlight and drive capacity improvements.
 What You'll Do: 
 Own Production Scheduling & Execution 
 · Own discrete production scheduling and job sequencing across work centers to maximize on-time delivery and throughput.
 · Own work order release to the floor and control what work is released and when.
 · Set and manage priority and milestone dates, establish clear, transparent rules for what runs when, and make the trade-off calls when priorities conflict.
 · Own data integrity for schedules and dates in the system, and maintain and drive accurate MRP schedules so plans, priorities, and downstream commitments can be trusted.
 · Build the daily/weekly scheduling cadence and standard work that keeps the floor aligned, from shift-level execution to weekly look-ahead.
 · Translate S&OP network allocation and capacity plans into an executable, sequenced factory schedule.
 · Partner closely with the site General Manager to align on priorities, sequencing, and daily execution serving as the GM's right hand for turning the plan into on-time output.
 · Establish the system and cadence for tracking work order progress through the floor, monitors status against milestone dates, surfaces at risk jobs early, and drives rapid recovery on exceptions.
 Drive OTD & Factory Performance 
 Own on time delivery as a primary metric track it, root cause misses, and close the gaps.

 Ensure the factory is set up for success: materials, tooling, capacity, and priorities aligned ahead of the work, not discovered at the machine.

 Highlight and drive capacity improvements — surface constraints and bottlenecks from real execution data and partner with Operations and Engineering to resolve them.

 Feed execution signal (actual cycle times, constraints, attainment) back to S&OP to sharpen capacity models and sellable-capacity commitments.

 Build Methodology, Rigor & Visibility 
 Develop the scheduling methodologies and logic from the ground up, sequencing rules, buffering, prioritization frameworks and codify them as standard work applied consistently across sites.

 Establish communication rigor: the meeting cadence, escalation paths, and reporting that keep the floor, the GMs, and leadership on the same page.

 Build the visual management schedules, boards, dashboards, and status views that make factory status, priorities, and risks obvious at a glance.

 Establish key scheduling metrics: OTD, schedule adherence, past due, work center utilization, and cycle time performance.

 People Leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planners and schedulers as the function scales, including team members embedded at and dotted lined to the sites.

 Build organizational capability through talent development, standard work, training, and performance management.

 Foster a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

 Qualifications 
 · Proven experience in production planning, scheduling, or shop floor operations management in a discrete manufacturing environment.
 · Deep understanding of production scheduling, sequencing, priority management, master scheduling, capacity/constraint analysis, and OTD drivers.
 · Hands on experience with scheduling/ERP/MES systems and strong analytical and data visualization skills.
 · Experience leading teams and developing planning/scheduling talent.
 · Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to drive urgency and accountability on the floor.
 · ERP/MRP expertise work order lifecycle, MRP mechanics, and maintaining schedule/date data integrity at scale.
 Education & Experience Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline preferred.

 5+ years of progressive experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations.

 Benefits for Full-time Employees
 Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
401k 

 Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 Flexible vacation policy 

 Equity

  
 ITAR Requirements
 To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.
  
 Use of AI in hiring
 Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy .
  
 Consideration of Criminal History
 Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.
  
 Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer
 Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.
